title: Toxicological evaluation of some antimicrobials, antioxidants, emulsifiers, stabilizers, flour-treatment agents, acids and bases
authors: Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives
journal: FAO Nutrition Meetings Report Series 40A,B,C; WHO/Food Add./67.29; ninth (Rome, 13 to 20 December 1965) and tenth (Geneva, 11 to 18 October 1966) meetings; entries for carbonates, hydroxides and oxides
funder: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and World Health Organization.
result: Sodium carbonate (Na2CO3·xH2O, not less than 99.0% Na2CO3 after drying) is used as a neutralizing agent; sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO3, baking soda, not less than 99.0% after drying) as a neutralizing and leavening agent. Evaluation covering these and the other listed carbonates, hydroxides and oxides: 'Provided the nutritional implications or the over-all dietary intake of cations derived from these additives are taken into account, there appear to be no toxicological grounds to limit their use in accordance with good manufacturing practice.'
